uncited: It solves the problem of insufficient geometric constraints by introducing external priors—such as geometry scaffolds, visibility maps, or semantic masks—to regularize the implicit density and color fields.

What sets these methods apart from standard NeRF training is the explicit injection of structural or visibility information before or during optimization, rather than relying solely on photometric consistency across views.
All methods in this family share the goal of stabilizing the optimization of the implicit function $\sigma(\mathbf{x})$ and $\mathbf{c}(\mathbf{x}, \mathbf{d})$ under data scarcity.
The challenge of sparse-view NeRF reconstruction has been a significant focus in computer vision, as standard NeRF requires dense sampling to resolve the ambiguity between density and color.
Early works like [NeRFVS](8667-nerfvs.md) and [ViP-NeRF](8690-vip-nerf.md) introduced geometric and visibility priors to mitigate floaters and blurring in indoor and general scenes.

Concurrently, methods like [Sparse NeRF Reconstruction with Geometric and Semantic Initialization](8779-sparse-nerf-reconstruction-with-geometric-and-semantic-initi.md) leveraged traditional computer vision pipelines (COLMAP, Mask R-CNN) to bootstrap the implicit representation.
